Orca Security Plugin for Antigravity

Cloud security context from Orca, inside your Antigravity agent.

## What it does Connects Antigravity's agent to the [Orca Security MCP server](https://orca.security/mcp-server/), so it can triage alerts, explore assets and attack paths, query your cloud inventory, track compliance, and search cloud detection events using live data from your Orca account. ### What you can ask for - **Alerts:** find, filter and triage alerts. Read an alert's details, timeline, attack path and AI agent findings. Change its status or score, snooze it, or add comments. - **Assets:** look up cloud assets by name or ID. See the alerts and attack paths that touch them, and mark crown jewels. - **Attack paths:** explore how an attacker could reach your most sensitive assets. - **Vulnerabilities:** check whether a CVE affects your environment, and look it up in Orca's CVE catalog. - **Compliance:** review enabled frameworks, failed controls and posture trends per account or business unit. - **Cloud detection and response (CDR):** search and group cloud audit events. - **Orca AI agents:** list the agents available for an alert, run them, and read their results. - **Documentation:** search Orca's product documentation. Every action runs with your own Orca user's permissions. ## Requirements - An Orca Security account - The Antigravity App or the `agy` CLI ## Install **Antigravity CLI** (recommended) ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/orcasecurity/antigravity-plugin ``` Verify with `agy plugin list`. **Manual** Clone the repo into the global plugins folder: ```bash git clone https://github.com/orcasecurity/antigravity-plugin ~/.gemini/config/plugins/orca-security ``` To scope the plugin to one project, clone it into that workspace's `.agents/plugins/` folder instead. The plugin then shows under **Customizations** > **Installed**.
Manual MCP setup (without the plugin) If you prefer not to install the plugin, add the server to `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "orca-security": { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.orcasecurity.io" } } } ``` In the Antigravity IDE you can open the same file from the agent panel: **...** > **MCP Servers** > **Manage MCP Servers** > **View raw config**.
## Sign in The plugin uses OAuth and needs no configuration, so it installs enabled. When its MCP server first connects, Antigravity prompts you to sign in with your Orca account in the browser. No client ID or secret is needed. If you need to sign in again, go to **Customizations** > **Installed** > **MCP Servers** and click **Authenticate**. In the `agy` CLI, sign in from `/plugin` > **Installed** > **orca-security** > **Sign in**.
Use an Orca API token instead of OAuth Add this server to `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`, using your regional URL if your account isn't in the US (for example `https://api.eu.orcasecurity.io/mcp`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "orca-security-token": { "serverUrl": "https://api.orcasecurity.io/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Token YOUR_ORCA_TOKEN" } } } } ```
## Try it - Show my top critical alerts in Orca - Which attack paths lead to my most sensitive assets? - What is my compliance status for CIS AWS Foundations? ## What's in this repo ``` . ├── plugin.json Plugin manifest ├── mcp_config.json Orca MCP server definition ├── assets/logo.png Plugin logo ├── SECURITY.md How to report vulnerabilities └── LICENSE MIT license ``` ## Privacy [Orca Security Privacy Policy](https://orca.security/privacy-policy/) ## Support - **Email:** mcp@orca.security - **Docs:** https://docs.orcasecurity.io/docs/mcp-integration ## Security To report a vulnerability, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
